properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL — Anthony, 2026-08-31, proposing three ways to break the hub monolith: Interface Segregation (split `impl DesignGraph` into smaller traits), Data-Context-Interaction (treat DesignGraph as pure data, move hanging methods into contextual worker modules), and Sub-graph Views (a `ReadGraphView` for queriers, a `MutationGraphView` for mutators). Nothing chosen.

⭐⭐ THE FINDING, MEASURED 2026-08-31: ALL THREE ALREADY EXIST HERE, AS ONE MECHANISM, AND IT REACHES 3 OF 45 MODULES.

`crates/reflow2-core/src/graph_read.rs` declares `pub trait GraphRead` — five functions: get_node, scan_nodes, count_nodes, outgoing, and one more. `DesignGraph` implements it. That IS the interface segregation, and it is also the read view.

AND THE MIGRATION PATTERN IS ESTABLISHED, applied three times:
    pub fn confirmation_ledger(g: &dyn GraphRead) -> Result<ConfirmationLedger, DynoError>
    pub fn granularity_report(g: &dyn GraphRead)  -> Result<GranularityReport, DynoError>
    (coverage.rs the third)
A free function over the contract, with a one-line `impl DesignGraph` block left behind as a delegating wrapper so no caller breaks. THAT IS THE DCI SHAPE — pure data, behaviour in a contextual worker — arrived at independently and already in the tree.

AND THERE IS A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION, WHICH IS THE PART THAT PROVES THE SEAM IS REAL: `CountingRead<'_>`, a decorator. Its own words: "before this there was no way to ask what a module costs the store without editing the module. Now any module behind the contract can be measured from the outside, by construction, without touching it... wrap a real graph, a test fake, or another decorator, and the module under measurement cannot tell."

═══ ⭐ THE CONSEQUENCE THAT TIES THIS TO THE OPTIMISE THREAD ═══
`CountingRead` is what makes `con:granularity-reads-scale-with-artifacts-not-edges` (N+2 store reads) MEASURABLE AT ALL. So the read seam is not merely tidier structure — IT IS THE MEASUREMENT LEG FOR PER-MODULE OPTIMISATION. That is exactly the thing Anthony wanted from "optimise inside a black box", and it is available today for any module that sits behind the contract and unavailable for any that does not.

⇒ So the honest reframe: the architecture question looks settled and the open question is REACH. 3 of 45 modules are behind the contract; 42 still take `&self` on the shared struct.

═══ THE NUMBERS THAT MAKE IT TRACTABLE ═══
    78  `&self` methods on DesignGraph   (read)
    16  `&mut self` methods              (write)
    45  modules adding methods to the struct, 62 impl blocks
     5  functions on GraphRead
     2  implementations (DesignGraph, CountingRead)
     3  modules migrated
The surface is 83% read, so a read view covers most of it, and a `MutationGraphView` — the half that does NOT exist — would be a 16-method problem rather than a 94-method one.

═══ THE OPTIONS, none chosen ═══
① MIGRATE MODULES ONTO `GraphRead`, worst-first, using the established three-step pattern. Incremental, reversible, each step independently valuable because it makes that module measurable. No new architecture. Bounded by 42.
② BUILD THE WRITE HALF — a `MutationGraphView` over the 16 `&mut self` methods, completing the read/write split he drew. Smaller than the read side and gives the write path the same measurability.
③ WIDEN `GraphRead` FIRST. Five functions may not cover what the 42 need; some will want traversal or index access that is not there. Measuring what they actually call, before migrating, would say whether five is enough.
④ DO NOTHING AND LET IT SPREAD BY DEMAND — migrate a module only when somebody needs to measure or fake it. Cheapest; leaves the reach permanently low, which is how it got to 3 of 45.

⚠️ COUNTER-ARGUMENTS, recorded beside rather than used to argue it down. (1) `dec:the-graph-read-contract-stays-internal` (ACCEPTED, his word 2026-08-21) settles that this boundary is INTERNAL, not published — modular is not the same as published, and widening its reach must not be read as a commitment to outsiders. (2) Nothing has yet been BLOCKED by a module not being behind the contract; the case for migration is measurability, not a defect. (3) `&dyn GraphRead` is dynamic dispatch on the hottest read path in the system, and no measurement here says what that costs — the optimize skill would demand that number before a mass migration, not after.
properties.name: OPEN — ISP / DCI / read-write views are all already built here as GraphRead, reaching 3 of 45 modules; is the work migration rather than architecture?
